title: The Six Great Faiths
welcome_lead: Travel the globe and meet the six major world religions that shape billions of lives.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure exploring the six major world religions and their global followings.
final_note: You've mapped the world's six major faiths and their billions of followers.

concepts.def: Largest religion, around 2.4 billion followers worldwide.
Second largest religion, around 1.9 billion followers.
Ancient religion of India, around 1.2 billion followers.
Founded by Siddhartha Gautama, around 500 million followers.
Founded by Guru Nanak, around 30 million followers.
Oldest Abrahamic faith, around 15 million followers.

walkthroughs.body_html: By number of followers, the six major world religions rank: Christianity (~2.4bn), Islam (~1.9bn), Hinduism (~1.2bn), Buddhism (~500m), Sikhism (~30m), Judaism (~15m). Together they cover most of the world's religious population.

Three faiths began in the Middle East: Judaism, Christianity and Islam (the Abrahamic religions). Three began in India: Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism (the Dharmic religions). Each spread across the world through trade, migration and missionaries.

Although different, world religions often share ideas: a moral code, sacred writings, places of worship, and rituals marking birth, marriage and death. Studying them helps us understand cultures and history.
